hazard: Inadequate documentation of patient condition and decisions
theme: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

reports.title: Evelyn Ross
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: The inquest was told that the ward in question had been short staffed for a number of months. As a result there was a reliance on agency staff and less experienced staff. The trust was now seeking to resolve the issue but it was still not fully resolved. It reflected a wider issue of a national shortage of nurses.
concerns.hazard: staffing shortages leading to reliance on agency and less experienced staff

concerns.quote: The inquest was told that whilst Mrs Ross was medically fit for discharge prior to 1st July she had not been discharged because of delays in arranging a suitable care package to support her in the community.
concerns.hazard: delayed discharge due to lack of community care package

concerns.quote: During the course of the inquest the documentation relied on by the trust was lacking in detail and meant that it was difficult to understand her condition at key points or to understand the rationale for decisions.
concerns.hazard: inadequate documentation of patient condition and decisions

concerns.quote: The inquest heard that the Trust had not followed their own falls risk policy in relation to Mrs Ross.

There did not appear to be a clear system of regular orthogeriatric consultant reviews of Mrs Ross. This meant that there was no escalation of her condition to a consultant when she began to show signs of deterioration.
concerns.hazard: absence of regular orthogeriatric consultant reviews

reports.title: Chloe Every: Prevention of Future Deaths Report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: BHRUT plan to recruit more learning disability nurses in 2025. They have created pathways to encourage and upskill existing staff due to the shortage of nurses going into learning disability training (RNLD).
promises.summary: Recruit and upskill learning disability nurses by 2025

concerns.quote: The Trust does not provide nursing cover during weekends and holiday periods of staff with relevant learning disability training.
concerns.hazard: lack of nursing cover during weekends and holidays for staff with relevant learning disability training

concerns.quote: The investigation of this inquest was prejudiced by the absence of contemporary nursing and medical notes from various stages of Chloe's treatment. The extent of these lapses meant staff who made important treatment decisions could not be identified, and where staff could be identified, no contemporary account of their rationale for making treatment decisions could be located.
concerns.hazard: absence of contemporary nursing and medical notes

concerns.quote: The regularity of Chloe's clinical observations fell well below the expected level. The lapses included a period of over 10 hours in which no observations were undertaken.

Chloe underwent an enema on 8th May 2019 without informed consent being taken. The court found that Chloe was unconscious, before, during, and after the procedure, it is possible this procedure contributed to her death.
concerns.hazard: enema performed without informed consent on unconscious patient

concerns.quote: Nursing staff were incapable of explaining to the court the appropriate criteria that would have to exist before commencing CPR on an unresponsive patient.

Governance processes at the Trust failed to identify that Chloe's death constituted a patient safety incident until months after her death. A mortality review authored by the Associate Medical Director on 17th May 2019 assessed Chloe's care as good or excellent.
concerns.hazard: governance failure to identify patient safety incident
